FSEC (Faculty Senate Executive Committee) Special Meeting Minutes Date: Wednesday September 9, 2026 - Time: 10:00 am to 11:00 Pastore Hall Room 224 - Remote option via ZOOM Find the Acronym Glossary here 1. Call to Order - Pres. Preisser called the special meeting to order at 10:03 pm. VP Trimm and Senators Van Wyk, Daniels, Meyerson, and Chen were present. 2. Minutes for approval 2.1 Minutes of the 8/31/26 FSEC meeting. The minutes were approved. 3. Priority Items and 3.1. Orientation - Planning for the 9/10 meeting - FSEC reviewed a script keyed to slides that corresponded with the various agenda items. Several edits were offered to both the script and the slides. Staff will revise and redistribute so that all FSEC members (and the Parliamentarian) can prepare for their roles. 3.2. Planning for the 9/17 meeting - The agenda was reviewed and finalized as it will need to be posted before the next FSEC meeting. It was approved unanimously. Staff will continue to organize slides as the various presentations come in and will add line numbers to all legislation. Back-up for two of the bills will be appended directly to the bill drafts so multiple attachments will not be necessary. It was noted that the summer curriculum committee chair is no longer a senator, but she will be invited to attend the 9/17 meeting in case there are questions about the reports. CASC Liaison Trimm will coordinate with her. 4. Updates/Ongoing Items 4.1. Timely Updates, if needed - It was noted that the next FSEC meeting will be Wed. 9/16, the day before the next senate meeting. That agenda will largely revolve around detailed meeting prep for the 9/17 meeting. 5. New Business – Open for additional items not listed in the agenda. None 6. Adjournment - The meeting adjourned at 11:10 am.

FSEC (Faculty Senate Executive Committee) Meeting Minutes Date: Wednesday September 16, 2026 - Time: 10:00 am to 12:00 Pastore Hall Room 224 - Remote option via ZOOM Find the Acronym Glossary here Action Items: Staff will work with the FS President to clean up slides and scripts for the 9/17 FS meeting.
Pres.
Preisser will continue to refine the JCODL bill amendment language in advance of the meeting.
Staff will start reaching out to potential speakers/presenters tentatively scheduled for the October senate meeting so that the agenda can be firmed up. 1.
Call to Order - Pres.
Preisser called the special meeting to order at 10:01 pm.
VP Trimm and Senators Van Wyk, Daniels, Meyerson, and Chen were present. 2.
Minutes for approval 2.1 Minutes of the 9/9/26 FSEC meeting.
The minutes were approved. 3.
Priority Items and New Business 3.1.
Recap - 9/10 senate meeting - FSEC members were pleased with how the Orientation event went.
Although the attendance felt sparse in the room, there were a number of attendees on Zoom and staff confirmed that nearly all newly elected senators were on hand.

The idea of providing Orientation purely for new members was discussed with the pros being that experienced senators will not feel pressured to attend during the demanding first week of classes, and such a protocol would help adjust the expectation that the room will be full of senators, which it typically is not for Orientation. 3.2.
Meeting Prep - 9/17/26 Faculty Senate Meeting - see also microphone duties.
The spreadsheet showing microphone responsibilities was shared and staff noted a hard copy will always be in the meeting room.
The agenda and accompanying slides were discussed in detail.
Regarding the curricular reports, it was noted that SSCC Chair Furong Xu will be on hand to answer any questions about summer approvals.
Several announcements were added for inclusion before FSEC moved on to discuss specific legislation. 3.2.1 Discuss Proposed Legislation: ● Reintroduction of JCODL Legislation - VP Trimm will act as presiding officer during this item as Pres.
Preisser will present the legislation substantively.
Amendments have been proposed, which Pres.
Preisser has discussed with the proposer, and draft alternative text is being inserted into the slides for presentation.

Staff will prepare electronic ballots in case a voice vote is inadequate for determining approval of the proposal and related amendments. ● Course withdrawals legislation and back-up - It was noted that the current proposal applies to regular session courses only.
There were suggestions regarding clarity on some of the slides and it was questioned whether a faculty member’s signature indicated an approval or simply an acknowledgment of withdrawal.
Pres.
Preisser noted that one important take-away from this agenda item will be that good ideas for enactment by the senate can come from anywhere on campus, not just from faculty members (the bill was proposed by an advisor in CELS). 1

● Special/Standing Committees - This draft is not expected to be controversial and the slides are forthcoming. 3.3.
Current Project Tracker and Advance Agenda Setting updates - The October senate meeting agenda was briefly discussed so that advance notice to various presenters can be provided. 3.4.
Committee Assignment Updates 3.6.1 Standing Committee Members - An additional senator has resigned since the draft list was finalized.
The COB has been advised to run a special election and transmit the results asap.
New member committee placements will need to be ratified in a future senate meeting. 3.6.2 Joint Committees - Still a work in progress - Staff is still waiting to hear back from some candidates for joint committee assignments.
A list of appointments will be approved at the 9/17 FS meeting, but it will not be complete and the senate will need to circle back to some placements in October.
Of particular note is the need to round out the CRCA membership as non-senator faculty are to be appointed by the VP RED and recruitment has proven challenging. 4.
Continued Items 4.1.
Faculty Concerns submitted through the FS Webpage - No new concerns were submitted. 4.2.

Chapter 3 Revisions needed - update - Because staff is waiting for some final proof-reading by affected departments, the informational report on revisions will be held until the October senate meeting. 4.3.
Continued Discussion - Creation of College Liaisons - No new update. 4.4.
Continued Discussion - Creation of a Programs Subcommittee (current draft) - VP Trimm had drafted a brief problem statement and a one paragraph “proposed solution” to provide the senate with a starting point to understand FSEC’s idea related to reconfiguring the curriculum committees.
The statements were reviewed and edited and will be used when the senate conducts a forum on the topic later this fall.
In particular, membership in the proposed programs subcommittee was discussed and FSEC agreed there are non-faculty members who are not Assoc.
Deans who might bring valuable perspectives to the committee.
The Manual language should provide enough flexibility for their appointment.
It will be important to stress that any new subcommittee will report to CASC and be SOLELY advisory to that standing committee.

It was noted that Associate Deans serving on the new subcommittee will likely need to be advised that their role in this regard is one of substantive curriculum review and not one related to making budget decisions.
Potential names of a new subcommittee were also discussed and “the SCUP” was suggested (Special Committee on Undergraduate Programs).
Legislation to create the new subcommittee, if approved, would take effect fall 2027. 5.
Updates/Ongoing Items 5.1.
Updates i.
Meetings with Administrators, Committees, or Others - The FS President and VP met with the University President, Provost and Vice Provost.
The discussion focused largely on the development of a medical school.
They also touched on the new idea for a brief presentation during the “land acknowledgment” part of 2

the senate meeting agendas. The administration is supportive so long as the presentations add something to the conversation and are in addition to, rather than a replacement of, the current land acknowledgement language, which cannot be altered. 6. Report of the Coordinator 6.1 Scheduling Guests - Staff is starting to process requests for an audience with the FSEC in their weekly meetings. If FSEC members have other ideas for special appearances or if they know of a committee chair who needs time with the full FSEC, they are encouraged to coordinate with staff. 7. New Business – Open for additional items not listed in the agenda. Senator Daniels briefly outlined a concern and asked that it be addressed in more detail at the next meeting. It involves a complication that his PhD students often run into. Part time graduate students are frequently on the receiving end of enrollment holds related to their academic progress because the university’s systems don’t readily accommodate part-time PhD candidates. Sen. Daniels has spoken to the new Graduate School Dean to express this concern on behalf of his students and now seeks FSEC’s guidance on other steps that might be taken. 8. Closing Remarks – Recap of decisions made, action items, and plans for the next meeting. FS Pres. Preisser reminded FSEC members that senate meetings are an opportunity for senators to be heard on important issues. Because FSEC members have the opportunity to debate weekly, they should defer to other speakers to the extent possible during the monthly meetings. 9. Adjournment - The meeting adjourned at 11:56 am. 3

FSEC (Faculty Senate Executive Committee) Meeting Minutes Date: Wednesday September 23, 2026 - Time: 10:00 am to 12:00 Pastore Hall Room 224 - Remote option via ZOOM Find the Acronym Glossary here Action Items: Sen.
Van Wyk will share the FS meeting schedule with Silvermoon LaRose so that plans for monthly land acknowledgment-related presentations can be planned for each AY 26-27 senate meetings.
Staff will reach out to the CBUM Chair to see if the committee can wait for the COB special election to play out, or if he prefers that FSEC pull a specific senator from another committee to serve on CBUM immediately.
Staff will reach out to the five candidates to serve on the Nominating Committee to determine their interest and ability to serve.
Pres.
Preisser will get the details of the specific Kuali workflow to understand the role(s) of the Harrington Director/A&S Assoc.
Dean and approach the A&S Dean if it is determined that there is the potential for a conflict of interest .
Sen.
Van Wyk will approach SSIREP’s new Director about potential collaboration with the URI-IFSA. 1.
Call to Order - Pres.
Preisser called the special meeting to order at 10:03 pm.

VP Trimm and Senators Van Wyk, Daniels, Meyerson, and Chen were present. 2.
Minutes for approval - Tabled to the 9/30 meeting. 2.1 Minutes of the 9/16/26 FSEC meeting 2.2 Minutes of the 9/17/26 FS meeting 3.
Priority Items and New Business (50 minutes) 3.1.
Recap - 9/17 senate meeting - FSEC members shared positive feedback about the efficiency of the meeting.
They noted that, following some initial trepidation from the administration about the new approach to the Land Acknowledgment, the presentation was actually very well received.
Sen.
Van Wyk will serve as Liaison to Ms.
LaRose and the students who will offer brief monthly presentations going forward.
There was a brief discussion of the University President’s budget report and it was noted that the mid-year report that occurs each January typically offers more detail about where the university stands with regard to both revenue and expenditures.
It was noted that the funds being used for early stage Medical School development are separate from the standard operating budget.

It is unknown to what degree that model will persist as the medical school becomes operational (for example, will corporate partnership funds and/or research grant indirects flow to the university as a whole, or just to the medical school?). 3.2.
Meeting Prep - 10/15/26 Faculty Senate Meeting - see also microphone duties - The draft agenda will be discussed in detail at the next meeting.
Staff noted that the annual enrollment update will not be ready in time for 10/15 and will be docketed for 11/19 instead.
This should free up some time on the October agenda for an additional ‘forum’ if needed. 3.2.1 Status of Legislation: ● Course withdrawals legislation and back-up - The draft legislation has been sent to CBUM and FSEC agreed that it should also be sent to TAAC and ACC for review and comment. ● Special/Standing Committees - The draft legislation as introduced on 9/17 has been sent to CBUM for review and comment. 1

3.2.2 Selection of Nominating Committee - Committee members must be drawn from among senators whose terms are expiring at the end of the academic year.
The list of eligible candidates was reviewed.
Several nominations were made and staff will reach out to the candidates to determine their interest and ability to serve. 3.2.1 Forum - Curriculum Committee Reorganization - A forum to gather input to inform future legislation will be held in November or December. 3.3.
Current Project Tracker and Advance Agenda Setting updates - Tabled. 3.4.
Committee Assignment Updates - Staff noted that two senators had resigned since standing committee assignments were drafted.
One has been replaced but the other has not.
CBUM has expressed an urgent need for an additional member.
Staff will reach out to the Chair to see if the committee can wait for the special election to play out, or if they prefer to pull a senator from another committee immediately. 3.4.1 Joint Committees - Still a work in progress.
Tabled to 9/30.

FSEC voted unanimously to enter Executive Session at 10:40 am to discuss college level shared governance concerns, especially in terms of impacts on academic freedom for faculty, and the limits of Deans’ authority over curricular matters. 4.
Continued Items - FSEC reconvened in regular session at 11:35am 4.1.
Graduate student-related concern as introduced last week - Sen.
Daniels noted that three of four of his PhD students are part-time.
They run into a bureaucratic hassle every year when enrollment holds are imposed due to the timelines associated with time to degree completion/rate of academic progress being made.
Forms and procedures required to release the holds are byzantine and archaic.
Sen.
Daniels has discussed the problem with the new Graduate School Dean who agreed that this should be addressed.
FSEC members were unsure if the UM and Enrollment Services protocols even provide for part-time status for these students but agreed that there should be a way to treat these students differently for enrollment purposes than the current system allows.
Sen.
Daniels will look into this a little more before the next meeting when the conversation will continue. 4.2.

Faculty Concerns submitted through the FS Webpage - Two new concerns had been submitted.
One pertained to whether or not an inherent conflict exists when a School Director also serves as an associate dean.
FSEC opinions diverged but it was agreed that Deans have broad authority and discretion in the Assoc.
Dean appointments.
It was also noted that in terms of promotion and tenure, the Director role does differ from that of a department chair.
FS Pres.
Preisser concluded that the primary area of concern from the perspective of the faculty senate would be the Assoc.
Dean’s role in curricular proposal processing.
Pres.
Preisser will get the details of the specific workflow and approach the appropriate Dean if it is determined that the Director/Assoc.
Dean is playing too many roles in the process.
The other concern was a suggestion that Sen.
Van Wyk’s IFSA initiative (survey design assistance) collaborate with the SSIREP.
Sen.
Van Wyk noted she had discussed potential partnership with the prior SSIREP Director, who was not interested.
She will approach the new Director as suggested. 2

4.3. Continued Discussions - The following were tabled to 9/30. 4.3.1 Creation of College Liaisons (evolution of draft: 2025 - 2026) 4.3.2 Creation of a Programs Subcommittee (current draft) 5. Updates/Ongoing Items - Tabled 5.1. Updates i. Meetings with Administrators, Committees, or Others ii. Other Updates 6. Report of the Coordinator - Tabled 7. New Business – Open for additional items not listed in the agenda. None 8. Closing Remarks – Recap of decisions made, action items, and plans for the next meeting. None. 9. Adjournment - The meeting adjourned at 11:50 am. 3

FSEC (Faculty Senate Executive Committee) Meeting Minutes Date: Wednesday September 30, 2026 - Time: 10:00 am to 12:00 Pastore Hall Room 224 Remote option via ZOOM Find the Acronym Glossary here Action Items: Staff will remind the senate of Saturday’s apple picking event.
Staff will work with the FS President to refine the draft special/standing committees legislation in advance of the 10/15 FS meeting.
Now that some legislative progress is being made, staff will update the FSEC’s project and priority tracker accordingly.
Re: the informational report on Chapter 5, staff will update the bill accordingly with the correction offered by CBUM and transmit back to the proposer for affirmation of language.
RE: the information report on Chapter 3, staff will work with the FS President to address CBUM’s concerns with the language.
In terms of advance planning, staff will invite the facilities group to provide an update to the senate on current and future construction projects at the November meeting. 1.
Call to Order - Pres.
Preisser called the meeting to order at 10:03 pm.
VP Trimm and Senators Van Wyk, Daniels, Meyerson, and Chen were present.
Past President Travis Williams was also on hand. 2.

Minutes for approval 2.1 Minutes of the 9/16/26 and 9/23/26 FSEC meetings.
The minutes were approved as edited. 2.2 Minutes of the 9/17/26 FS meeting - The minutes were tabled to the next meeting. 3.
Priority Items and New Business 3.1.
Meeting Prep - 10/15/26 Faculty Senate Meeting - The 10/15 agenda was discussed in detail but FSEC agreed to discuss the particulars of the proposed forum on college liaisons next week. 3.1.1 Status of Legislation: In terms of informational reports, several efforts in the editorial update to Chapter 3 were identified.
Staff will ‘ground-truth’ the draft with Kuali and the university catalog.
It was noted that websites, college by-laws, and other sources of information are also often in error or out of date.
The legislation can only address the catalog and manual but colleges can certainly be reminded to keep all sources of information as current as possible, to avoid confusing or misleading their students.

Regarding the other informational report (Chapter 5, correcting titles and terms in the section dealing with the PSAC), one correction was offered as part of CBUM’s review and staff will update the bill accordingly. ● Course withdrawals legislation and back-up - It was noted that the bill proposer has received a lot of feedback, both from senators at the 9/17 meeting and from CBUM.
She also has received formal comments from TAAC and will attend their next meeting on 10/22 to discuss modifications to the language.
Some of the questions/concerns relate more to the forms than the UM language.
The bill is not expected to be decided at the October meeting because the meeting with TAAC will not occur until after the 10/15 FS meeting.
A vote on the legislation will be tabled to 11/19. ● Special/Standing Committees - Suggestions for ‘friendly amendments’ from senators will be incorporated into a revised draft.
Sen.
Meyerson, who serves as 1

CBUM liaison, reviewed that committee’s comments on the proposal.
Some suggestions (clarifying assessment and reauthorization protocols, for example) can be easily addressed in the draft, but other concerns are more appropriately addressed by the specific charges and legislation creating new committees, wherein inclusion of effective dates, dates of eligibility for permanent status, etc. should be inserted.
Other suggestions, like offering a web presence for special committees, are well taken and staff noted that the FS office does include special committees among those listed on the website so that information on membership, charge, and progress reports is readily available.
Staff will work with the FS President to refine the draft legislation. 3.2.2 Selection of Nominating Committee - update - The committee is required to have three members and two people have agreed to serve.
A third has been asked but has not responded.
An alternate can be pursued if the third nominee declines. 3.2.1 Forum - College Liaisons - Tabled to next week. 3.2.
Current Project Tracker and Advance Agenda Setting updates - a couple of updates were made in the advance agenda template.

FSEC revisited their priorities for the year and staff will update the tracker accordingly.
The FS President spoke to Dean Libutti regarding his decision to move the admissions report from the October 2026 meeting to the November 2026 meeting.
Dean explained that this change was necessitated because the very early date (10/15) of this year's FS meeting did not allow time for his office to prepare a report beforehand.
The 'default' for future admissions reports will continue to be October. 3.3.
Committee Assignment Updates 3.6.1 Standing Committee Members - updates - There are two committee assignments that were not addressed by the senate’s 9/17 ratification of committee memberships.
At least one of these will be ready for action on 10/15.
The other depends upon the timing of a COB special election. 3.6.2 Joint Committees - Two committees (SAC and JCSC) are still in need of a member and nominees have been slow to respond about their willingness to serve.
The CRCA (not a Joint Committee, but some appointments are not made by the senate) is still in need of five non-senator, research-active faculty.
Two have been recruited and inquiries to others are awaiting responses. 4.

Continued Items (25 minutes) 4.1.
Graduate student-related concerns - follow up - Sen.
Daniels noted that part-time graduate students are addressed in four sections in the University Manual but their status is not defined (except through their exclusion from the defined class of full-time students).
He has met with the Graduate School Dean about the need to provide explicit definitions and guidance regarding part-time students so that Enrollment Services does not continue to impose enrollment holds on them.
Although the graduate school dean is very good about getting the holds lifted, they should not be happening in the first place.
FSEC members suggested other programs wherein students might be affected like Sen.
Daniels students are and it was suggested he collaborate with them as well as the Grad School Dean’s office to find a solution.
He will continue working and report back. 4.2.
Faculty Concerns submitted through the FS Webpage - There was one new concern that related to the length of time that paper exams/quizzes are required to be retained.
Sen. 2

Chen confirmed that there is language in the University Manual, Chapter 8, Section 52, that requires tests to be retained for two semesters after the end of the semester in which the test was given.
This information will be reported out at the October senate meeting.
Sen.
Van Wyk provided an update on a previously reported concern, which can also be addressed as an announcement at the October senate meeting. 4.3.
Continued Discussion - Creation of College Liaisons - The planned forum on this topic will be addressed in detail at the 10/7 meeting. 4.4.
Ongoing Discussion - Creation of a Programs Subcommittee - Senate VP Trimm is taking the lead on planning a future forum (probably December) wherein feedback from the senate is solicited before any specific proposal is introduced. 5.
Updates/Ongoing Items 5.1.
Updates i.
Meetings with Administrators, Committees, or Others ● CBUM meeting of 9/28/26 (LM) - Discussed as part of Item 3.1 above. ii.
Other Updates - Budget; College level governance concerns, etc.

It was noted that the FS President and FS staff had responded this week to inquiries regarding the past practice of transferring funds to the FS budget mid-year to cover FS officer course releases.
FSEC moved into Executive Session to address an ongoing college level governance issue regarding Senate oversight over curricular matters . 6.
Report of the Coordinator - None 7.
New Business – Open for additional items not listed in the agenda. 7.1 Curricular Practical Training (CPT) concerns - Senator Daniels noted that recent guidance from DHS is causing confusion and concern around student internships, especially with regard to the level of scrutiny the agency can give to the necessity of the work experience as an integral part of the curriculum.
There are differing interpretations within the colleges and departments about what DHS actually requires, and whether internships must be required as part of a degree program, or if the option of an internship as just one of several paths to program completion is sufficient to meet the DHS standard.
It is expected that the Office of General Counsel will weigh in on the approach the University should take.

FSEC members agreed that a crucial perspective to bring to bear in this inquiry would be that of Vice Provost for Global Initiatives Kristin Johnson.
It was suggested that she be approached as a partner in gleaning clear and comprehensive guidance about how to proceed.
Past President Williams noted that this seems to be an area in which the role of the faculty senate is not a formal one, i.e. it is not within the senate’s jurisdiction.
The senate can and should, however, play an informal role by focusing attention and energy on the issue and facilitating an exchange of information that might help the university solve the problem.
Past President Williams added that the FSEC should be guided by three central questions as they consider whether or not to advance an issue: 1) what is the problem? 2) What does a solution look like?
And 3) What can the senate do to achieve the solution, i.e. what is the appropriate level and type of senate involvement?
FSEC members agreed this is a good framework for figuring out how to triage and prioritize new issues and concerns. 8.
Adjournment.
The meeting adjourned at 11:50 am. 3

a specified topic)

Who may attend Faculty Senate meetings and where are they held?
Any member of the URl community or the general public may attend a Faculty Senate
meeting.However,only voting members of the Senate may vote on legislation,resolutions,
officer elections,and any other business raised at the meeting.Bylaws stipulate that only
Senators and ex officio members have the RIGHT to speak during meetings.Exofficio
members participate in discussions,ask questions,and make and second motions;theyare
not,however,allowed tovote.Non-senators may request to speak at a meeting beforehand
via the online Permission To Speak”form found on the Faculty Senate website.To facilitate
the meeting itself
Meetings take place throughout the academic year in the Hope Roomof the Higgins
Welcome Center from3-5p.m.monthly on a Thursday.A brief reception with refreshments is
provided at every meeting.This is a wonderful opportunity for in-person attendees to network
colleges
How are agenda items determined?
The meeting agenda is set by the Faculty Senate Executive Committee.Agenda items may
can also be suggested to the Executive Committee via an anonymous form on the Faculty

can also be suggested by a committee or introduced at a Senate meeting during the New
Business'portion.
While agenda items maybe suggested at anytime,inclusion of an item at the monthly
meeting requires the Executive Committee approve adding it to the agenda atleast one week
in advance of the scheduled senate meeting.This is necessary for timely agenda posting and
motion in realtime are typically considered for inclusion on a future agenda or referred to a
standing or special committee for further exploration.Exceptions to this timeline are reserved
for unusually urgent or time-sensitive Issues.
Doesthe Faculty Senate use parliamentary procedures to conduct meetings?
The Senate relies upon the American Institute of Parliamentarians Standard Codeof
Parliamentary Procedure.Guidebooks and other reference materials are available in the
Faculty Senate Office.Training on procedural basics is provided during the annual
Orientation meeting.This meeting is held each September and is required for all new
Senators(and highly recommended as a refresher for ALL Senators).
